instruction: Expand the volume slider's maximum setting to 200% instead of the current 125%.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing VLC's maximum volume setting from default 125% to 200%. The evaluator uses the existing check_qt_max_volume metric function to verify that qt-max-volume=200 is set in the VLC config file (~/.config/vlc/vlcrc). The get_vlc_config getter reads the config file and the metric checks if the qt-max-volume setting matches 200. No new functions needed - reusing existing VLC evaluation infrastructure.
metadata.similarity_to_original: Very similar - both tasks involve changing a single VLC preference setting through the UI. Original disables splash cone icon, this changes max volume limit.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement to change VLC max volume to 200%
get_vlc_config getter properly reads VLC config file (~/.config/vlc/vlcrc) and returns cached path
check_qt_max_volume metric correctly parses config file for 'qt-max-volume=' setting and compares to expected value 200
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter - directly accesses rule['expected_qt_max_volume'] since framework passes rules dict when expected.type='rule'
Expected value of 200 is semantically correct for the task (changing from default 125% to 200%)
Postconfig appropriately restarts VLC to ensure fresh config state before verification
Complete coverage - instruction has single requirement (set max volume to 200%) and evaluator checks exactly that
Edge cases handled: config file not found returns 0, missing setting uses default '125' for comparison
Data flow is correct: getter extracts config -> metric parses qt-max-volume setting -> compares to expected 200
